title: Primary succession
caption: On bare ground pioneer species such as lichens and mosses colonise first and begin forming soil. Each stage changes conditions so that new species can establish: soil depth, nutrients and water retention increase, until a stable climax community, often woodland in the UK, forms. Grazing or burning can hold it back (deflected succession).
alt: Five boxes in order: bare rock or sand, pioneer species, grasses and small plants, shrubs, and the climax community.
description: Bare rock or sand: no soil.
Pioneer species: lichens and mosses colonise and begin to form soil.
Grasses and small plants: soil deepens and holds more water and nutrients.
Shrubs: more shade and soil: more species arrive.
Climax community: stable woodland in the UK.
